definition: Momentary means lasting only an instant.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word momentary. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know momentary should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: A momentary hush fell over the courtroom as the foreman rose to speak, and then everyone spoke at once.
A short delay might still cost you ten minutes; momentary shrinks the claim to a single instant.
Split-second goes past momentary — over before you can even register that it began.

Brief promises only that something is short, and it is roomy: a brief meeting can still run twenty minutes, a brief visit an afternoon. Momentary narrows the claim to a single instant, over almost as it begins. Every momentary thing is brief, but very little that is brief is truly momentary.

Flickering means appearing and disappearing in quick pulses — a flame in a draft, a weak radio signal that keeps dropping out and coming back. A momentary thing happens once and is gone for good; whatever returns again and again is flickering, not momentary.

The sled gathered momentum on the long hill and could not be stopped at the bottom.
Momentary means lasting only an instant.
The photograph that made her name shows a heron, a leaping fish, and the rising sun stacked in one line — an alignment that was momentary in the strictest sense.
She had anchored the boat at that bend for six straight sunrises; the seventh gave her the picture, and by the time the shutter reset, the fish was down and the line was broken forever.
Momentary is the exact word because it names what lasts only an instant — not merely short, but over almost as it begins.
An intermission is short; a flash of alignment, a catch of breath, a shadow crossing a field is momentary.
And note the trap waiting one letter away: momentous means important, a different word entirely.
Momentary is for what lasts a single instant.

Its cluster-mates in this unit divide the longer stretches: ephemeral gives a thing a short but whole life — a day, one summer of fame — while transitory merely denies permanence, however slowly it goes.
And do not mistake momentary for momentous, which means important.

The flash is momentary, and blinking at the wrong time is enough to miss the whole show.
For a week she set her camera on the seawall each evening and watched the sun drop toward the Pacific through haze that ruined the view.
On the eighth evening the air was clean, and it came: a bead of pure green that appeared and was gone within a single heartbeat.
Her camera, firing ten frames a second, caught it on exactly one frame — the sky's whole performance, over before her breath was.
